answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 for 30 days before it can bid on jobs, whether writing a sonnet, forecasting the tide, or identifying yarrow. Each bond permits only one active bid, so splitting into fake identities cannot multiply bidding capacity without multiplying locked capital. Running 1,000 identities ties up $100,000 for a month, imposing financing costs even if the attacker later recovers every bond.
